$comment: Operator decision log (scripts/analysis/decision-log.mjs; Spec 124 R-HK). Question, recommendation and decision are the review page rows export docs/reports/decisions/raw/2026-10-20-bylaw-fix-rulings/2026-10-20-page-bylaw-rulings.json, verbatim. `decision_vocab`, `routing` (the register and row that record each decision), `amendments` and `options` are added by the lane and are not the operator's text; everything else is re-derived from `source.raw` by `--check`.

decisions.question: The Eglinton exemption (10.10.40.71(1)) is for a transportation use, not houses. Scope it to that use so it stops blanking front setbacks on house lots.

Give each projecting element its own encroachment target (eaves, window projections, porches, stairs) and let one rule carry both the maximum projection and the minimum clearance. Eaves: up to 0.9 m, no closer than 0.3 m to a lot line.

A garage rule (10.10.60.20(1)(A): 1.0 m from a rear or side lot line abutting a street or lane) applies to the garage itself. The user is asked whether the ancillary building holds a parking space; until answered, the result is "needs user input".
"In all other cases" arms take the opposite of their sibling arm's condition. First use: 10.5.60.50(2)(B), 40 m² total ancillary floor area when frontage is under 12 m.

When deciding a target is "unregulated" (nothing in the by-law limits it), ignore clauses that only define how to measure, and clauses that limit a different building type. Five new absence rulings close the last 16 open cells, including RM houseplexes answering "not applicable" for length, depth and main wall.
Let the decision log record "no ruling needed" items (CHAT-12 settled, CHAT-13 bug fix) as a new meaning, no_ruling, which must name the existing ruling it rests on.
